change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The driver torque response latency threshold for accelerator pedal demand above 70% was tightened from 100 ms to 80 ms, requiring updated test criteria and re-execution.

assessments.reason: The test directly verifies VCU-DR-01 with a procedure threshold of 100 ms. The previous measured result of 94 ms fails the new 80 ms specification limit.
assessments.recommended_action: Update the script threshold to 80 ms and rerun the test to establish valid evidence.

assessments.reason: The test directly links to VCU-DR-01 and applies an 85% pedal step, but previous execution did not record timing data to confirm compliance with the new 80 ms limit.
evidence: Comment notes timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: Rerun the test to record torque response latency and evaluate against the 80 ms requirement.

assessments.reason: The procedure sweeps pedal demand above 70% and previously recorded 92 ms, but its requirement link is missing. The recorded 92 ms fails the new 80 ms requirement.
evidence: Previous result was 92 ms exceeding 80 ms limit
assessments.recommended_action: Confirm linkage to VCU-DR-01 with system engineering, update procedure tolerance to 80 ms, and rerun the test.

assessments.reason: The test measures brake command latency under VCU-BRK-03, which operates on a different measurement clock and is independent of driver positive torque response timing.
evidence: Workshop note states brake latency and positive torque latency use different clocks

assessments.reason: This test verifies wheel-speed sensor fault handling and degraded mode operation under VCU-DGN-04, which is unchanged.
evidence: Checks degraded mode and diagnostic logging

assessments.reason: This test verifies timestamping and build logging for mode changes under VCU-LOG-05, which is unaffected by VCU-DR-01.
The procedure applies an 80% pedal step under thermal load, touching VCU-DR-01 behavior, but has a TBD link and unassigned ownership.
assessments.recommended_action: Clarify test ownership and confirm requirement linkage before defining pass criteria and scheduling execution.

assessments.reason: This test replays a legacy diagnostic trace linked to unknown requirement VCU-OLD-88 and does not evaluate driver torque latency.
The test evaluates Sport vs Comfort accelerator torque ramps under VCU-MOD-06, but does not currently include quantitative response latency assertions.
evidence: Comment notes no quantitative response-time assertion
assessments.recommended_action: Review with owner whether to add an explicit 80 ms latency check for Sport mode pedal steps above 70%.

assessments.reason: This test verifies input spike filtering under VCU-DR-02 using a 7 ms pulse and does not measure valid torque response latency.
This test verifies emergency brake priority over positive propulsion torque under VCU-BRK-03, which remains unchanged.
evidence: Verifies positive torque suppression on brake input

assessments.reason: This test verifies ECU startup readiness latency after power-up and has no relation to driver torque response time.
